subject: Post-call: Medicore private hosting constraints and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Medicore private hosting constraints and acceptance criteria

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured the acceptance criteria and the blockers you called out. Please flag anything I missed.

Key goals (Medicore):
- Keep PHI and PII in-region (US East) with no cross-border backups.
- Strong network isolation: on-prem-like, outbound-only egress through a corporate proxy/gateway.
- Auditability: streaming audit logs and access records to your SIEM (Splunk).
- Deterministic latency for inference within 120ms p95 for primary workloads.

Main constraints you highlighted:
- Air-gap requirement for test+staging environments; production can have controlled egress but must pass your legal checklist.
- No persistent third-party-managed storage outside the region; any long-term model artifacts need to live in your AWS account.
- Strict allowlist model for outgoing IPs; no DNS-based big-bang exceptions.

Technical assumptions from our side:
- Private deployment via Redwood Private (VPC peering or PrivateLink) with customer-managed VPC and KMS/HSM integration.
- Option to run model weights inside your account (we can ship an on-prem package) or to run in Redwood-owned tenants with strict tenancy and RU encryption — you indicated preference for weights in your account if feasible.

Open questions / clarifications needed from Medicore:
1) Which environments require complete air-gap (no egress) vs. controlled egress? A simple mapping (dev/test/prod) would help.
2) Do you have an internal egress gateway/proxy we should target for allowlist and outbound TLS termination? If so, can you share IP ranges and proxy hostname?
3) KMS/HSM: do you require HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) for model key material, or is KMS with CMKs sufficient?
4) Splunk ingestion: preferred ingestion endpoint and authentication method (Hec token, TLS client cert)?

Next steps we propose:
- Ben will draft a minimal network diagram and proposed allowlist (attached).
- Medicore security to confirm egress hosts and KMS preference (Elena — can you loop security?).
- Redwood to prepare a short SOW draft for a Proof-of-Concept (30 days) that scopes control plane access, key ownership, and SLAs; attached draft for review.

Attachments: medicore-network-sketch.pdf (diagram), redwood-private-hosting-sow-draft_v1.pdf (SOW draft)

Thanks — I’ll wait for the security contact and the env mapping and then Ben and I will iterate the SOW.

— Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicore.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Medicore Security <security@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Medicore private hosting constraints and acceptance criteria

Thanks Mina — helpful summary. Quick answers inline.

• Air-gap mapping: test (air-gapped, no egress), pre-prod (controlled egress for telemetry only), prod (controlled egress with allowlist).
• We have an outbound proxy/gateway (egress.prod.medicore.internal) and customer-managed NATs. I’ll share the IP ranges and the proxy host by close of day tomorrow.
• KMS: we require HSM-backed keys for any persistent model encryption. CloudHSM available in our AWS account.
• Splunk: we use HEC with token auth; will share endpoint and a service token via our secure vault.

Couple of clarifying points / asks:
- For air-gapped test, do you provide an offline installer that our infra team can bump into an isolated subnet? If so, what ports (if any) does it expect during install?
- We need a short checklist of evidence you can provide for SOC2-type controls and data handling for the POC.

Looping in security for the IPs and token.

— Elena
Head of Infrastructure | Medicore

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Medicore Security <security@medicore.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Medicore private hosting constraints and acceptance criteria

Elena — perfect, that mapping helps a lot. Short answers below and a couple of proposed timelines.

Air-gapped installer: yes — we can provide an offline installer package (containerized) that your infra team deploys into an isolated subnet. It requires:
- No inbound public ports.
- Outbound only to an internal KMS endpoint if you choose to configure remote wrapping; otherwise fully offline is supported.
- During offline install we need console access (SSH) to the host running the installer for the initial bootstrap. If your policy disallows SSH, we can provide a step-by-step op manual and support via an on-site/secure remote session.

Evidence pack for POC: we can provide
- SOC2 type control mappings (control IDs + description).
- Network diagrams and deployment guide.
- Redacted audit log samples and retention policy.
- Encryption-at-rest and in-transit descriptions and key handling docs.

Proposed POC timeline:
- Day 0–5: Procurement & account setup (IAM roles, CloudHSM provisioning).
- Day 6–12: Network allowlist and private connectivity (VPC peering/PrivateLink).
- Day 13–22: Installer deployment, key material import, smoke tests.
- Day 23–30: Performance profiling and SLA verification; final acceptance.

If that looks reasonable we’ll turn the SOW into an executable POC SOW and schedule a technical kickoff with your infra/security team next week. Ben — can you take the network diagram and expand the allowlist with suggested CIDR exceptions and proxy egress points? Laura — can you prepare the evidence pack outline so we can attach it to the SOW.

Thanks — Mina

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medicore.com>, Medicore Security <security@medicore.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Network allowlist and install notes (attachment)

Elena / Security team — attaching an initial allowlist + install notes (medicore-network-sketch.pdf). Highlights:
- Outbound IPs to allow: 34.201.12.0/24 (control plane), 52.23.45.128/25 (telemetry ingestion).
- Installer ports: outbound TLS (443) only for optional telemetry; SSH 22 is optional for bootstrap if you want remote support.
- For fully air-gapped installs: follow steps in section 2 of the doc to import the container bundle via a secure artifact exchange (no egress required).

I also added a short note on CloudHSM integration and the recommended key wrap flow (we will not escrow unencrypted model weights). If you prefer, we can make the POC run with model artifacts stored entirely in your S3 buckets and keys in your CloudHSM-backed KMS.

Next: Elena — once you share the proxy host and ranges I’ll finalize the CIDR list and update the SOW.

— Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
